K-th Shortest Routes

You are an intelligence operative maintaining a high-frequency trading (HFT) network spanning N geographically sparse server hubs and M unidirectional fiber optics lines.

Finding the absolute fastest path for a trade order isn't enough; rival firms frequently DDOS your primary lines. To ensure split-second fallback capability, you must constantly compute the top K fastest data routes from the main exchange (hub 1) to the execution server (hub N).

Note that routes are permitted to contain cycles if navigating a cycle is the only way to achieve a marginally slower secondary path.

Output exactly K lines, containing the travel times of 1st, 2nd... up to the K-th shortest paths. If fewer than K distinct path instantiations exist, output -1 for the remaining missing ranks.
explanation: This is solving the 'K Shortest Paths' (with cycles) algorithm. Since positive weights are guaranteed, we can employ an augmented Dijkstra's Algorithm (functioning similar to A* search evaluating uniform costs). Instead of maintaining a solitary shortest distance array, we simply count the number of visits to each node. We permit a node to be visited and re-expanded up to K times. Once the destination node has been reached K times, we have verifiably discovered our top K shortest paths. Wait, the time complexity scales directly with K * E log(K*V), cleanly circumventing the immense complexity of finding only simple paths. Path tracking efficiently limits to array pushes.
